classification.difficultyReason: Students connect successive derivatives to three motion graphs, distinguish speed from signed velocity, and explain non-zero acceleration at an instant of rest. The quadratic flight calculations and maximum-height method are already scaffolded by the teaching.

content.prompt: A cricket ball is thrown vertically upwards. Its height $x$ in metres at time $t$ seconds after it is thrown is given by $x=20t-5t^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find $v$ and $a$ as functions of $t$, and show that the ball is always accelerating downwards. Then sketch graphs of $x$, $v$ and $a$ against $t$.

answer.short: $x=5t(4-t)$, $v=20-10t\text{ m/s}$ and $a=-10\text{ m/s}^2$. The acceleration is always downwards. Graphs are shown for $0\le t\le4$.
answer.worked:
Taking upwards as positive,
$$\begin{align*}v(t)&=\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=20-10t,\\a(t)&=\frac{dv}{dt}\\&=-10.\end{align*}$$
Thus the acceleration is $10\text{ m/s}^2$ downwards throughout the flight.
$$\begin{align*}x(t)&=20t-5t^2\\&=5t(4-t).\end{align*}$$
The height graph crosses the time axis at $t=0$ and $t=4$, with maximum $(2,20)$. The velocity graph joins $(0,20)$ to $(4,-20)$ and crosses the time axis at $t=2$. The acceleration graph is horizontal at $a=-10$.

spec.description: Three complete native solution graphs in reading order: height above, velocity then acceleration below; all original paths, values, guides and labels retained.
spec.mathematics: For 0≤t≤4: x=20t−5t², vertex (2,20); v=20−10t, intercepts (0,20), (2,0), endpoint (4,−20); a=−10.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; no supplied graph appears in the student prompt.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the speed at which the ball was thrown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}v(0)&=20-10(0)\\&=20\text{ m/s}.\end{align*}$$
The initial speed is $|v(0)|=20\text{ m/s}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find when it returns to the ground (that is, when $x=0$) and show that its speed then is equal to the initial speed.

answer.short: It returns after $4\text{ s}$. Its speed then is $20\text{ m/s}$, equal to its initial speed.
answer.worked:
$$5t(4-t)=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=0\text{ or }4.$$
The return occurs at $t=4\text{ s}$, since $t=0$ is the launch.
$$v(4)=20-10(4)=-20\text{ m/s},\qquad |v(4)|=20\text{ m/s}=|v(0)|.$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find its maximum height above the ground and the time taken to reach this height.

answer.worked:
At the maximum height, $v=0$.
$$20-10t=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad t=2\text{ s}.$$
$$x(2)=20(2)-5(2)^2=20\text{ m}.$$
Since $a=-10<0$, this stationary height is a maximum.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Find the acceleration at the top of the flight, and explain why the acceleration can be non-zero when the ball is stationary.

answer.short: $-10\text{ m/s}^2$. The velocity is zero for an instant but is still changing.
answer.worked: $a(2)=-10\text{ m/s}^2$, or $10\text{ m/s}^2$ downwards. At the top, $v(2)=0$, but the velocity continues to decrease from positive to negative. Acceleration measures the rate of change of velocity, so it remains non-zero at that instant.
